messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity of the swinging body. Body dimensions, shape, and the viscosity of the surrounding medium are the other essential parameters. Parameters including fluid density and the surface area in contact with the fluid further influence the damping. Damping is quantified by a coefficient that relates the resistive force directly to the velocity. Velocity-proportional resistance defines the linear viscous drag model. Model equations for a physical pendulum must include this term when the oscillation occurs in a fluid such as air or water. Water or any other substantial fluid environment ensures that energy is continuously dissipated from the system. System behavior in a vacuum or extremely rarefied gas may neglect this effect, but under everyday conditions it must be included.
